docs.title: swipe
docs.text:
Run Claude Code with the right account for every directory. Work repos open with your work login, everything else with your personal one, and no alias to remember. One source tree holds your commands, hooks, agents and settings, so the two accounts stop drifting apart.

curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/octanelabsdev/swipe/main/install.sh | sh
echo 'eval "$(swipe init zsh)"' >> ~/.zshrc

Then tell it which folders belong to which account in ~/.config/swipe/profiles.json:

{
  "default": "personal",
  "profiles": {
    "personal": { "config_dir": "~/.claude" },
    "work": { "config_dir": "~/.claude-work", "paths": ["~/code/acme"] }
  }
}

Now claude in ~/code/acme uses your work account, and claude anywhere else uses your personal one. Full setup, including Windows and PowerShell, is in Install.

docs.title: Why this exists
docs.text:
Claude Code keeps everything for an account in one config directory: the login, settings, history, commands, hooks. Claude Code's docs recommend giving each account its own directory and pointing CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR at it. In practice that means:

  • an alias like claude-work you have to remember, and forget, and end up on the wrong account;
  • two copies of every command and hook, which quietly drift apart as you fix one and not the other;
  • nothing that works the same way on a teammate's Windows laptop.

swipe fixes all three:

Problem What swipe does Remembering which alias to use claude picks the account from the folder you're in Copies drifting apart Files live once in a source tree, linked into each account's directory Different machines and shells One binary for macOS, Linux and Windows; hooks for bash, zsh and PowerShell

docs.title: What it never touches
docs.text: Your logins, history, projects and anything else Claude Code writes for itself stay exactly where they are. swipe only manages files you put in its source tree, and it never overwrites or deletes a file it didn't create. See How it works.

docs.title: Where to go next
docs.text:
• Install

    The binary, the shell hook, and your first profiles.json.

  • Moving an existing setup

    Already have ~/.claude and ~/.claude-work? Import them without losing anything.

  • Sharing files between accounts

    One copy of each command, hook and setting, with per-account overrides.

  • Troubleshooting & FAQ

    Wrong account, conflicts, Windows symlinks, IDE extensions.

docs.title: Commands
docs.text:
Command What it does swipe run [args…] Starts claude with the profile for the current directory, passing args through swipe which [dir] Prints the profile and config directory for dir (default: the current directory) swipe sync Builds every profile's config directory from the source tree swipe import <profile> Copies a profile's existing files into the source tree, then syncs them back swipe init <shell> Prints the shell hook: bash, zsh or powershell swipe help Prints usage swipe --version Prints the version

Every command exits with status 0 on success, 1 on an error or conflict, and 2 for a usage error. swipe run exits with claude's own status.

docs.title: swipe run
docs.text:
swipe run --resume

The shell hook makes claude an alias for swipe run, so you normally never type it. It resolves the profile, prints swipe: <profile> (<config dir>) to the terminal, and starts the first claude on your PATH (on Windows, also claude.cmd and other PATHEXT extensions). If the profile can't be resolved, claude isn't started.

docs.title: swipe which
docs.text:
$ swipe which ~/code/acme/api
work    /Users/you/.claude-work

Prints the profile name and config directory, separated by a tab. Useful in scripts:

CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR=$(swipe which | cut -f2)

Warning

For a profile whose config_dir is ~/.claude, leave CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR unset instead. On macOS, setting it explicitly points Claude Code at a different login.

docs.title: swipe sync
docs.text: Links every file in shared/ and profiles/<name>/ into each profile's config directory, merges settings.json, and removes what it placed that's no longer in the source. It reports conflicts instead of overwriting anything it didn't create. See Sharing files between accounts.

docs.title: swipe import <profile>
docs.text: Copies CLAUDE.md, settings.json, keybindings.json, agents/, commands/, hooks/, output-styles/ and skills/ from the profile's config directory into profiles/<profile>/, then syncs that profile. Nothing is deleted. Links to folders, git repos, skills/synced/, skills/.trash/ and .venv, node_modules and __pycache__ folders are left in place. See Moving an existing setup.

docs.title: swipe init <shell>
docs.text:
Prints the hook to add to your shell's startup file:

bash / zshPowerShell 
unalias claude 2>/dev/null || true
function claude { command swipe run "$@"; }

Remove-Item Alias:claude -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
function claude { swipe run @args }

docs.title: One config directory per account
docs.text:
Claude Code stores each account's login, settings and history in a config directory. The default is ~/.claude; setting the CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR environment variable points Claude Code at a different one. Claude Code's authentication docs recommend exactly this for keeping a work and a personal account signed in side by side.

Where the login is kept depends on the platform:

Platform Login stored in macOS The Keychain, in an entry tied to the config directory's path Linux .credentials.json inside the config directory Windows .credentials.json inside the config directory

swipe never reads or moves any of this. It only decides which directory Claude Code gets.

docs.title: Picking a profile
docs.text:
When you run claude, the shell hook runs swipe run, which:

  1. resolves the current directory to its real path, following symlinks and using the folder's real letter case;
  2. finds every profile with a paths entry containing it, and picks the most specific one;
  3. falls back to default if nothing matches;
  4. starts the real claude with CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR set to that profile's config_dir.

The ~/.claude profile

For a profile whose config_dir is ~/.claude, swipe unsets CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR instead of setting it. On macOS, the login is tied to whether the variable is set and to its exact value. Setting it to ~/.claude explicitly would make Claude Code look for a different login, and you'd appear logged out.

If two profiles match equally well, for example because one lists a folder and another lists a symlink to the same folder, swipe refuses to guess and reports both. If the configuration is invalid or no profile matches and there's no default, claude isn't started at all, so you never end up on the wrong account by accident.

On macOS and Linux, swipe run replaces itself with claude, so signals, exit codes and the terminal behave exactly as if you'd started claude directly. On Windows it starts claude, waits for it, and passes its exit code through.

docs.title: The source tree (optional)
docs.text:
Choosing the account is all most people need. If you also want your commands, hooks and settings kept in one place, swipe sync builds each config directory from a source tree:

~/.config/swipe/
├── profiles.json
├── shared/                 # goes into every profile
│   ├── commands/review.md
│   ├── hooks/notify.sh
│   └── settings.json
└── profiles/
    └── work/               # only for the work profile; wins over shared/
        ├── CLAUDE.md
        └── settings.json

Details in Sharing files between accounts.

docs.title: What swipe will never do
docs.text:
• Read, copy or move your logins, history, projects, or anything else Claude Code writes for itself.
  • Overwrite or delete a file it didn't create. It reports a conflict instead and leaves the file alone.
  • Write or delete through a symlinked folder inside a config directory.

docs.title: profiles.json
docs.text:
swipe reads profiles.json from its source tree:

Platform Default location macOS, Linux ~/.config/swipe/profiles.json Windows %USERPROFILE%\.config\swipe\profiles.json

Set SWIPE_HOME to use a different folder, for example a dotfiles repo. If SWIPE_HOME isn't set and XDG_CONFIG_HOME is, swipe uses $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/swipe.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
{
  "default": "personal",
  "profiles": {
    "personal": { "config_dir": "~/.claude" },
    "work": {
      "config_dir": "~/.claude-work",
      "paths": ["~/code/acme", "~/code/acme-infra"]
    },
    "client": {
      "config_dir": "~/.claude-client",
      "paths": ["~/code/acme/client-portal"]
    }
  }
}

Here ~/code/acme/api uses work, ~/code/acme/client-portal/web uses client (its path is more specific), and everything else uses personal.

docs.title: default
docs.text: Optional. The profile to use when no profile's paths contain the current directory. It must name a profile defined below. Without it, claude refuses to start outside a listed folder.

docs.title: profiles
docs.text: Required. An object mapping each profile name to its settings.

docs.title: config_dir
docs.text:
Required. The Claude Code config directory for this profile. It must be absolute or start with ~. No two profiles may share one.

Use the same spelling you already log in with

On macOS, Claude Code ties the login to the exact CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR value. If you've been using CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR=$HOME/.claude-work, write ~/.claude-work, not a symlinked or differently cased path, or Claude Code will ask you to log in again.

docs.title: paths
docs.text:
Optional. Folders that use this profile, including everything under them. Each must be absolute or start with ~.

  • The most specific match wins.
  • Paths are matched by real location: symlinks are followed, and letter case is ignored on macOS and Windows.
  • A path that doesn't exist, or can't be read, is skipped.
  • Two profiles can't list the same path.

docs.title: Validation
docs.text: swipe checks the whole file on every run and stops with an error naming the problem: unknown keys (so a typo like "path" can't silently switch accounts), wrong types, relative paths, a shared config_dir, a duplicate path, or a default that doesn't exist.

docs.title: Environment variables
docs.text: Variable Effect SWIPE_HOME Source tree location (contains profiles.json, shared/, profiles/) XDG_CONFIG_HOME Used as $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/swipe when SWIPE_HOME isn't set SWIPE_COPY=1 swipe sync copies files instead of symlinking them

docs.title: Install
docs.text: Setup has three steps: install the swipe binary, add the shell hook, and write a profiles.json.

docs.title: 1. Install the binary
docs.text:
swipe is a single binary with no dependencies.

macOS and LinuxWindowsWith Rust 
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/octanelabsdev/swipe/main/install.sh | sh

This installs swipe in ~/.local/bin. If that folder is not on your PATH, the script tells you the line to add.

irm https://raw.githubusercontent.com/octanelabsdev/swipe/main/install.ps1 | iex

This installs swipe.exe in %LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\swipe and adds that folder to your user PATH.

cargo install --git https://github.com/octanelabsdev/swipe

This needs Rust 1.88 or newer, and puts swipe in ~/.cargo/bin.

The scripts download the latest release from GitHub and check its SHA-256 checksum before they install anything. They don't need admin rights. To install a specific release, set SWIPE_VERSION (for example SWIPE_VERSION=v0.1.0). To use a different folder, set SWIPE_INSTALL_DIR.

Check that it works:

swipe --version

docs.title: 2. Add the shell hook
docs.text:
The hook defines a claude command that runs through swipe. swipe then starts the real claude with the right account. Add one line to your shell's startup file:

zshbashPowerShell 
echo 'eval "$(swipe init zsh)"' >> ~/.zshrc

echo 'eval "$(swipe init bash)"' >> ~/.bashrc

Add-Content $PROFILE 'swipe init powershell | Out-String | Invoke-Expression'

Open a new terminal afterwards. If you had an alias such as alias claude-work=... or alias claude=..., you can delete it. The hook removes any existing claude alias so it can't shadow the hook.

Git Bash on Windows

Git Bash uses the bash hook. cmd.exe has no shell functions, so it isn't supported; use PowerShell or Windows Terminal instead.

docs.title: 3. Write profiles.json
docs.text:
swipe reads ~/.config/swipe/profiles.json. Create it:

{
  "default": "personal",
  "profiles": {
    "personal": { "config_dir": "~/.claude" },
    "work": { "config_dir": "~/.claude-work", "paths": ["~/code/acme"] }
  }
}
  • config_dir is the Claude Code config directory for that account. ~/.claude is Claude Code's own default.
  • paths are the folders, and everything under them, that use this profile.
  • default is used everywhere else.

Every field is described in profiles.json.

docs.title: 4. Check it
docs.text:
cd ~/code/acme && swipe which
# work  /Users/you/.claude-work

cd ~ && swipe which
# personal  /Users/you/.claude

Then run claude as usual. A one-line banner names the profile it picked:

swipe: work (/Users/you/.claude-work)

The first time you use a new config directory, Claude Code asks you to log in to that account. After that, each directory keeps its own login.

docs.title: Updating and uninstalling
docs.text:
To update, run the install command again. It replaces the binary with the latest release.

To uninstall, delete the binary: ~/.local/bin/swipe, or %LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\swipe on Windows. If you installed with Rust, run cargo uninstall swipe.

To uninstall, also remove the hook line from your shell startup file. Your config directories are left exactly as they are; if you used swipe sync, see Sharing files between accounts first.

docs.title: Moving an existing setup
docs.text: You already have a ~/.claude and maybe a ~/.claude-work, each with its own commands, hooks and settings, and an alias to switch between them. This guide moves both into swipe without logging out or losing anything.

docs.title: 1. Back up
docs.text:
swipe import checks everything before it changes anything, but these are your working configs. Take a copy first:

macOS / LinuxWindows (PowerShell) 
tar -czf ~/claude-config-backup.tgz -C ~ .claude .claude-work

Compress-Archive -Path $HOME\.claude, $HOME\.claude-work -DestinationPath $HOME\claude-config-backup.zip

docs.title: 2. Describe your profiles
docs.text:
Install swipe and write profiles.json as in Install. Use the same config directories you use today, spelled the way your alias spells them. On macOS the login is tied to that exact path:

{
  "default": "personal",
  "profiles": {
    "personal": { "config_dir": "~/.claude" },
    "work": { "config_dir": "~/.claude-work", "paths": ["~/code/acme"] }
  }
}

At this point claude already picks the right account. Steps 3 and 4 are only needed if you want swipe to manage your files as well.

docs.title: 3. Import each profile
docs.text:
swipe import personal
swipe import work

For each profile, import takes the files you wrote yourself:

CLAUDE.md · settings.json · keybindings.json · agents/ · commands/ · hooks/ · output-styles/ · skills/

It copies them into profiles/<name>/ in the source tree, then syncs: each original that is identical to its new copy is swapped for a link to it, so Claude Code sees exactly what it saw before. Everything else in the config directory stays where it is: the login, history, projects, plugins and caches.

$ swipe import work
import /Users/you/.claude-work/CLAUDE.md
import /Users/you/.claude-work/commands
import /Users/you/.claude-work/settings.json
work (/Users/you/.claude-work)
  link /Users/you/.claude-work/CLAUDE.md -> /Users/you/.config/swipe/profiles/work/CLAUDE.md
  …

What makes it safe:

  • Nothing is deleted. An original is only ever replaced by a link to an identical copy. If the sync stops partway, for any reason, every file you haven't seen replaced is still there.
  • Before copying, it checks that your settings.json is valid JSON and a real file (not a symlink), and that nothing it would create in the source tree already exists. A broken symlink or unreadable file stops the copy. In every one of these cases nothing is changed at all.
  • Links to files stay links to the same file. Links to folders, such as a skill linked from another repo, are left exactly where they are, so they stay live. The import lists them as "left in place".
  • Git repos (any folder with a .git inside) are left in place too, so git keeps working.
  • Folders Claude Code fills in itself stay where they are: skills/synced/ (skills from claude.ai, which differ between accounts) and skills/.trash/. So do folders a tool rebuilds on each machine: .venv, node_modules and __pycache__.
  • A link from one of your files to another one in the same config directory is pointed at the imported copy. A link to something that isn't imported, such as history.jsonl, is left in place.
  • It refuses a profile that swipe has already placed files in.

When shared/settings.json already exists

If you import a profile after creating shared/settings.json, the merged result differs from the profile's current settings.json, so the sync reports a conflict and keeps the current file. Your settings are already safe in profiles/<name>/settings.json: delete the config directory's settings.json and run swipe sync to write the merged version. Importing every profile before creating shared/settings.json avoids this.

docs.title: 4. Share what's identical
docs.text:
After importing, both profiles have their own copy of everything. Move what's the same into shared/. This lists the files that are byte-for-byte identical in both:

cd ~/.config/swipe/profiles/personal
find . -type f -exec sh -c 'cmp -s "$1" "../work/$1" && echo "$1"' _ {} \;
cd ..

For each one, move a copy to shared/, delete both profile copies, then sync:

mkdir -p ../shared/commands
mv personal/commands/review.md ../shared/commands/review.md
rm work/commands/review.md
swipe sync

Files that differ stay in each profile. That's the right home for anything tied to one account, such as a hook that writes to a work-only folder.

docs.title: 5. Remove your old aliases
docs.text:
Delete alias claude-work=... and similar lines from your shell startup file and open a new terminal. Check both accounts:

cd ~/code/acme && claude    # swipe: work (...)
cd ~ && claude              # swipe: personal (...)

docs.title: 6. Keep the source tree somewhere safe
docs.text:
The source tree is now where your commands and settings live. Putting it under version control is a good idea:

cd ~/.config/swipe && git init && git add . && git commit -m "Claude Code profiles"

Before committing, check that no file contains secrets (API keys in settings.json env, for example).

docs.title: Undoing it
docs.text:
Restore the backup from step 1:

rm -rf ~/.claude-work && tar -xzf ~/claude-config-backup.tgz -C ~ .claude-work

Or keep the files and stop syncing, as described in Sharing files between accounts.

docs.title: Sharing files between accounts
docs.text: swipe sync builds each profile's config directory from one source tree, so a command or hook you fix once is fixed for every account.

docs.title: Layout
docs.text:
~/.config/swipe/
├── profiles.json
├── shared/                  # every profile gets these
│   ├── CLAUDE.md
│   ├── commands/review.md
│   ├── hooks/notify.sh
│   └── settings.json
└── profiles/
    ├── personal/            # only the personal profile
    │   └── commands/journal.md
    └── work/                # only the work profile
        ├── CLAUDE.md        # replaces shared/CLAUDE.md for work
        └── settings.json    # merged over shared/settings.json for work

Run swipe sync after adding, removing or renaming files. Edits to a file that's already synced show up straight away, because the config directory links to the source.

$ swipe sync
personal (/Users/you/.claude)
  link /Users/you/.claude/commands/review.md -> /Users/you/.config/swipe/shared/commands/review.md
work (/Users/you/.claude-work)
  link /Users/you/.claude-work/CLAUDE.md -> /Users/you/.config/swipe/profiles/work/CLAUDE.md
  write /Users/you/.claude-work/settings.json

A sync with nothing to do prints only the profile names. Running it twice in a row is always safe.

docs.title: The rules
docs.text:
Files. Every file under shared/ goes into every profile at the same relative path. A file at the same path under profiles/<name>/ replaces it for that profile. On macOS and Windows, paths that differ only in letter case count as the same path.

Links or copies. Files are symlinked to the source. Where symlinks aren't allowed, swipe copies them instead (see Windows). Copies keep the source's executable bit, so hook scripts still run.

Symlinks in the source are followed, so you can point shared/skills at a folder in another repo and its files are synced like any other.

Ignored names: .DS_Store, and the .swipe-manifest.json file swipe keeps in each config directory.

Removing. When a file leaves the source, the next sync removes the link or copy it made, and any folder that's left empty.

docs.title: settings.json
docs.text:
settings.json is merged instead of linked, because each profile usually needs a little of its own. swipe merges profiles/<name>/settings.json over shared/settings.json:

  • objects are merged key by key;
  • lists are combined, keeping the shared items first and adding the profile's new ones;
  • anything else from the profile replaces the shared value.
shared/settings.json
{ "model": "opus", "permissions": { "allow": ["Read", "Bash(ls:*)"] } }
profiles/work/settings.json
{ "model": "sonnet", "permissions": { "allow": ["Bash(git status)"] } }
~/.claude-work/settings.json (written by swipe)
{ "model": "sonnet", "permissions": { "allow": ["Read", "Bash(ls:*)", "Bash(git status)"] } }

The result is written as a real file. When both sources are removed, swipe removes the settings.json it wrote.

Edits made directly to settings.json

If anything edits the config directory's settings.json directly (you, Claude Code, or a tool that installs plugins), the next swipe sync notices and stops with a conflict for that file instead of overwriting it. Copy what you want to keep into your source settings.json, delete the config directory's settings.json, and sync again.

docs.title: Conflicts
docs.text:
swipe never overwrites or deletes something it didn't create. The one exception is a file that is byte-for-byte identical to its source (or a settings.json with the same JSON content): replacing it with a link loses nothing, so swipe does. Even then it moves the original aside first, and only deletes it once the link works; if anything fails, the original goes back. When something is in the way, it reports a conflict for that file, syncs everything else, and exits with status 1:

swipe: /Users/you/.claude/hooks/notify.sh: already exists or was edited in place; move what you
want to keep into /Users/you/.config/swipe, delete it, then re-run
Message Meaning Fix already exists or was edited in place A file is there that swipe didn't write, or a copy was edited Move it into the source tree (or delete it), then sync is a symlink not made by swipe Your own symlink is in the way Remove it, or move its target into the source tree is inside …, which is a symlink A folder in the config directory is a symlink; writing into it would change files elsewhere Replace the symlinked folder with a real one, or stop managing that folder is a directory A folder sits where a file should go Move or delete the folder was changed outside swipe settings.json was edited, by you or by Claude Code Fold the change into the source and delete the file leads back to this file The source file is a link to the very file in the config directory Replace the link in the source tree with the real file ….swipe-replacing is in the way A sync was interrupted while it replaced a file; this is the original Check it, keep what you need, delete it, then sync

docs.title: Windows
docs.text:
Creating symlinks on Windows needs Developer Mode (Settings → System → For developers) or an administrator shell. Without either, swipe copies files instead and says so once:

  symlinks are not allowed here, so swipe will copy files instead

Copies behave like links except that edits to the source only arrive on the next swipe sync. swipe remembers what it copied, so it updates its copies but never overwrites one you edited in place. Set SWIPE_COPY=1 to get copies on any platform.

docs.title: Stopping
docs.text:
To stop syncing a profile, delete .swipe-manifest.json from its config directory. Its links still point into the source tree, so either keep the source tree or replace the links with real files first:

# macOS and Linux: turn every link into the source tree into a real copy
SRC="$HOME/.config/swipe"
find ~/.claude -type l -lname "$SRC/*" -exec sh -c \
  'target=$(readlink "$1") && rm "$1" && cp -p "$target" "$1"' _ {} \;
rm ~/.claude/.swipe-manifest.json

Repeat for each config directory. On Windows without Developer Mode the files are already copies, so deleting .swipe-manifest.json is enough.

docs.title: Claude opened with the wrong account
docs.text:
Run swipe which in the same folder. If it names the wrong profile:

  • Check paths in profiles.json. The most specific matching path wins; a folder outside every path uses default.
  • swipe matches the folder's real location. If you reached it through a symlink, the link's target is what's matched.

If swipe which is right but Claude still uses the wrong account, the hook isn't active:

type claude      # bash/zsh: should say "claude is a shell function"

Get-Command claude   # PowerShell: CommandType should be Function

If it isn't, check that the swipe init line is in your startup file and open a new terminal.

docs.title: Claude asks me to log in again
docs.text:
Claude Code ties each login to its config directory, and on macOS to the directory's exact spelling. Make config_dir match what you used before: ~/.claude-work, not a symlinked or differently cased path. For the ~/.claude profile, swipe leaves CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR unset, which is what Claude Code expects for its default.

Claude Code's docs note one exception: Claude Console sign-ins made without an API key are stored outside the config directory, so separate directories don't keep two of them apart.

docs.title: The VS Code / JetBrains extension, or the desktop app, uses the wrong account
docs.text:
Those start Claude Code themselves and don't go through your shell, so the hook never runs. Set CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR in the editor's environment for that workspace if the editor supports it, or launch the editor from a terminal where you've set it:

CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR=$(swipe which | cut -f2) code .

For the ~/.claude profile, launch without setting it.

docs.title: "conflict" or "problem(s)" after swipe sync
docs.text: Something swipe didn't create is where it wants to put a file. Each line names the file and what to do. See the conflict table. Everything else was still synced.

docs.title: "broken symlink in source"
docs.text: A symlink in your source tree points at something that doesn't exist. swipe stops syncing that profile rather than guess. Fix or remove the link and sync again.

docs.title: "profiles … all match"
docs.text: Two profiles list paths that are the same folder on disk, often one through a symlink. Remove one, or make one more specific.

docs.title: Windows: files are copies, not links
docs.text: Without Developer Mode, Windows doesn't let normal users create symlinks, so swipe copies files. Turn on Developer Mode (Settings → System → For developers) and the next sync uses links for new files. Files that swipe already copied stay copies until they leave the source tree.

docs.title: cmd.exe
docs.text: cmd.exe has no shell functions, so there's no hook for it. Use PowerShell, Windows Terminal or Git Bash, or run swipe run directly.

docs.title: Can I keep the source tree in my dotfiles repo?
docs.text:
Yes. Set SWIPE_HOME to the folder in your shell startup file, before the swipe init line:

export SWIPE_HOME="$HOME/dotfiles/swipe"

docs.title: Does swipe send anything anywhere?
docs.text: No. It reads profiles.json and your source tree, and writes only inside the config directories it manages and, for import, the source tree.
